survey: A stone chess table set in a park, seen from the front and a little above, with three parts. 1) The table: a thick square slab of grey marble with a black-and-cream checkered board set into its top. The slab sits on a single central pedestal. The pedestal flares out under the slab like a capital, narrows into a shaft, then widens again into a stepped square base resting flat on the grass. The slab is centred on the pedestal and doesn't overhang too far for stone, so it could carry its weight. 2) The left stool: a round marble seat on a narrower drum with a wider ring at the base, sitting on the grass beside the table. 3) The right stool: the same shape and size as the left one, sitting in front and to the right of the table on the grass. Grass blades overlap the bottoms of all three pieces and each casts a shadow, so they touch the ground and don't float. Parts don't pass through each other, the round seats are round, and the two stools match. Two stools for a two-player game is the right number. The board is a flat inlay, so pieces could be played on it. Note: I couldn't reliably count the board squares at this size (each row may hold more than 8). If it isn't 8×8 that would be at most a minor point, since it is a simplified board.
